terms.gloss: once and again, more than once
evidence: Caes. BG 1.31: semel atque iterum armīs contendisse (Lewis & Short s.v. iterum)
Traupman 88: once or twice, semel atque iterum
terms.comment: Not a vague “once or twice” but “once and again, repeatedly”. Traupman 88 gives it for “once or twice”, which is semel aut iterum (below).

evidence: Cic. Brut. 308: semel aut iterum, only once or twice (Lewis & Short s.v. semel)

sources: Lewis & Short: semel
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 88, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
